title: Answer Partitions and Oracle Access Determine Quantum Query Complexity
summary: An answer partition specifies which oracle instances share an output, while query complexity also depends on how those instances are accessed. We formulate exact one-query answer-partition resolution as block discrimination of a unitary oracle family. Applied to Deutsch's problem with a controlled response unitary V, the criterion shows that one query suffices if and only if -1 is an eigenvalue of V; cyclic addition in odd response dimension therefore raises the exact quantum cost to two queries, matching the classical cost while preserving the same computational-basis point values.
